blocks.text: 1. Knowledge Graph RAG

blocks.alt: A structured schema builds a knowledge graph enabling structured queries

blocks.text: Multi-Hop RAG closed by weighing when its per-hop cost is worth it. Knowledge Graph RAG, retrieval grounded entirely in a pre-built structured graph, is the more formal, schema-driven end of the graph retrieval spectrum introduced generally in Graph RAG.
It queries a fully constructed knowledge graph directly rather than combining it with chunk retrieval.
2. Graph RAG As A General Idea, Knowledge Graph RAG As A Specific Implementation

blocks.alt: Graph RAG is a general idea while knowledge graph RAG is a specific implementation

blocks.text: Graph RAG names the general strategy of traversing relationships.
Knowledge graph RAG is one specific, fully structured implementation of that strategy.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Concept","Scope"],"rows":[["Graph RAG","General strategy of traversing entity relationships"],["Knowledge Graph RAG","A specific, fully schema-driven implementation"]]}

blocks.text: 3. A Structured Schema Defines Valid Relationships
Unlike an ad hoc extracted graph, a knowledge graph typically follows a defined schema of entity and relationship types.
A schema that constrains what relationships are even considered valid.
4. Querying Graph Databases With Structured Queries

blocks.alt: A question becomes a structured graph query against a graph database

blocks.text: As with traversal replacing similarity search in Graph RAG, a dedicated graph database is queried with a structured query language built for traversal.
This happens through structured traversal, not an embedding similarity comparison.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A dedicated graph query language built specifically for traversal retrieves connected entities directly by relationship type, a different mechanism entirely from comparing embedding vectors for similarity.

blocks.text: 5. Combining Structured Facts With Unstructured Text

blocks.alt: Structured facts combine with unstructured text

blocks.text: A knowledge graph node can still link back to the original unstructured passage it was extracted from.
Combining a precise structured fact with the richer natural language context around it.
6. Keeping The Graph Current As Facts Change
As with building the graph from documents in Graph RAG, a fact that changes after the graph is built leaves the graph stale.
An ongoing update process is required to keep the graph accurate over time.

blocks.content: {"headers":["State","What is required"],"rows":[["Graph built once","Accurate only until the next fact changes"],["Graph with ongoing updates","Stays accurate as source facts change over time"]]}

blocks.text: 7. Entity Resolution Across Sources

blocks.alt: One entity mention is checked against another for being the same entity

blocks.text: The same real world entity can appear under different names across different source documents.
Resolving those different mentions to one single graph node is real, ongoing work.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A company referred to as Falcon Cloud in one document and Falcon Cloud Services in another, must be resolved to the same graph node, or the graph ends up with duplicate, disconnected entities for the same real thing.

blocks.text: 8. Knowledge Graph Construction Is The Main Cost
As with graph construction is real engineering work in Graph RAG, building and maintaining a schema, extracting entities, and resolving duplicates is the dominant cost of this approach.
A meaningfully larger investment than the general graph RAG idea alone suggests.
9. Recognizing When Knowledge Graph RAG Earns Its Construction Cost

blocks.alt: A domain with rich structured relations points toward knowledge graph RAG

blocks.text: Domains with well defined entity types and relationships suit a formal knowledge graph.
Loosely structured, varied source material is better served by the lighter general graph RAG approach.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Building a knowledge graph without a defined schema, allowing arbitrary invalid relationships.
Skipping entity resolution and ending up with duplicate nodes for the same real entity.
Building the graph once and never updating it as underlying facts change.
Choosing full knowledge graph RAG for loosely structured data that suits general graph RAG better.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: Knowledge graph RAG retrieves entirely from a pre-built, structured knowledge graph.
Graph RAG is the general strategy; knowledge graph RAG is one specific, formal implementation.
A defined schema of entity and relationship types constrains what is considered valid.
Graph databases are queried with a structured traversal language, not embedding similarity.
Graph nodes can link back to the original unstructured text they were extracted from.
An ongoing update process is required to keep the graph accurate as facts change.
The same real entity can appear under different names, requiring entity resolution to one node.
Schema design, entity extraction, and entity resolution are the dominant cost of this approach.
